requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Judgment: the sources satisfy `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`.**

**Implementation (`src/outline/rust.rs`)**
- `KINDS` maps every item kind the requirement lists to an outline node:
  - functions and methods (`function_item`, plus `function_signature_item` for trait and extern signatures);
  - structs, enums, unions, traits, impls and modules;
  - macros (`macro_definition` as a named node, and item-position `macro_invocation` as an anonymous node);
  - constants, statics and type aliases (`type_item`, plus `associated_type`);
  - extern blocks (`foreign_mod_item`).
- Most named kinds take their name from the grammar `name` field, which gives `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]` and `mod[local]/fn[run]`. Nesting comes from the ancestry-based outline tree.
- `impl_name` names an impl by the syntactic self type as written, plus `/` and the trait path when present. That gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and for example `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- `extern_name` names an extern block by its ABI string, or `Rust` when there is none. This produces the documented `extern[C]`.
- `use_declaration` and item-position macro invocations use `NameRule::Anonymous`, so they get `kind@hash` selectors.
- `in_item_list` and `item_macro` limit macro nodes to item position. Expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes.
- Nothing in the code resolves modules across files. A selector is always relative to the one file being parsed.
- The code beyond the requirement's list is the `extern-crate` kind and the `associated_type` and `function_signature_item` mappings. All are documented in the profile table. They fit the requirement's "items", functions and type aliases, or the "named by a suitable name" rule. The requirement does not forbid them.
- The {impl} marks cover the Rust-specific parts: `impl_name`, `extern_name`, `in_item_list`, `item_macro`, `KINDS` and `PROFILE`. Generic selector mechanics (percent-encoding, `#N` suffixes, hashes) belong to other requirements and are not part of this one.

**Documentation (selector spelling)**
- `md/reference.md`, "Rust items", gives the Rust selector examples. They cover `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, `extern[C]/fn[puts]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.
- It also explains impl naming (`impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`), the anonymous `use@…` and item-position macro forms, and that modules are never resolved across files.
- The "Selectors" and "Outline profiles" sections add the general selector rules and a full Rust kind/name table.

**Tests (`src/outline/tests.rs`)**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks every required item kind and each selector spelling:
  - `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `mod[external]`, `struct[Thing]`, `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`;
  - a non-path self type, `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`, with percent-encoding;
  - `trait[Trait]/fn[read]` and `trait[Trait]/type[Item]`;
  - `extern[C]/fn[puts]` and `extern[Rust]/fn[other]` (no ABI string);
  - nested functions, duplicate-name `#1` and `#2` selectors, `macro[make]`, `union[U]`, `enum[E]`, `const[C]`, `static[S]`, `type[Alias]` and `extern-crate[core]`.
  - It also checks that selectors resolve back to their nodes, that an ambiguous selector such as `fn[repeated]` is an error, and that a missing selector is an error.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` covers anonymous `use@` selectors that differ between two `use` declarations, plus the main named cases.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` covers anonymous item macros at top level, in an impl and in a module. It also covers a generic impl name, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`, and shows that expression macros are not nodes.
- `functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file` is cited only against the example `selector_inline_and_foreign`, not this requirement. It shows `mod local;` and the module file's functions are not linked across files.
- `nodes_are_declared_on_their_name_line_or_where_their_syntax_starts` (cited against `requirements.cli.add_input_item`) additionally covers wrapped impl headers and `extern "system"`.

**Residual points, none of which are gaps**
- Unusual ABI literals, such as raw strings, are not tested.
- The cross-file non-resolution test is not directly cited against this requirement, but it is covered by the example.

No FIXME comments or acknowledged gaps were found.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
